title: Quadratic linearization remainder
statement: Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and let $f\colon E\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable at every point, with derivative $D(x)\colon E\to\mathbb R$ at $x$. Suppose $D$ is Lipschitz in operator norm with constant $C\geq0$. Then, for all $x,y\in E$, $\|f(y)-f(x)-D(x)(y-x)\|\leq C\|y-x\|^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is a real normed vector space
replaced: Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $D(x):E\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $x\mapsto D(x)$ is $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm, where $C\ge0$. For all $x,y\in E$, $|f(y)-f(x)-D(x)(y-x)|\le C\|y-x\|^2$.
